name: Dhamma Suttama

location.address: 810 Côte Azélie, Notre-Dame-de-Bonsecours, Montebello, Quebec J0V 1L0, Canada

tradition: Vipassana Meditation as taught by S.N. Goenka
technique: Anapana (breath awareness) followed by Vipassana body-scanning meditation, taught in silent, structured ten-day residential courses via recorded instructions and evening discourses from S.N. Goenka
teacherAccess: No individual teacher access; courses are conducted using audio and video recordings of the late S.N. Goenka's instructions and discourses, with certified assistant teachers on site to answer meditation-related questions.
retreatOptions: Ten-day residential Vipassana courses offered nearly year-round (two per month, the centre's standard and primary offering), plus periodic longer courses for qualified old students and dedicated children's and teenagers' courses.
about: Dhamma Suttama, also known as the Quebec Vipassana Centre, is the Goenka-tradition Vipassana centre for Quebec, set on a secluded 600-acre property in its own valley about 5 km north of Montebello, halfway between Montreal and Gatineau/Ottawa. Courses were first offered in eastern Canada from rented sites starting in 1979; students purchased a permanent centre in Sutton in 1999, then this larger, nearly turnkey property - a former private co-educational high school - in 2011 once the Sutton site outgrew demand. The main building holds dining rooms and a professional kitchen, and two meditation halls in the former gymnasium each seat about 75 students, alongside attached dormitory-style residences with double and private bedrooms. Owned and operated by the nonprofit Eastern Canada Vipassana Foundation, the centre offers residential ten-day Vipassana courses as taught by S.N. Goenka in the tradition of Sayagyi U Ba Khin, nearly twice a month year-round, accepting up to about 130 students per course. Students live on site for the full course, observe Noble Silence, and follow the standard Goenka daily schedule; as at every centre in the Goenka network, there are no fees of any kind - courses, food and lodging are offered purely on a dana (voluntary donation) basis by past students.
schedule: Standard Goenka ten-day course schedule: arrival evening begins the course, followed by ten full days of silent sitting meditation (roughly 4am-9pm) with recorded evening discourses, and departure the following morning; Noble Silence is observed by all new students for most of the course.
cost: No fees of any kind; entirely dana (voluntary donation)-based, in keeping with the worldwide Goenka Vipassana tradition - all teaching, food and accommodation are offered freely, funded by donations from past students.

pricePerDay.notes: No suggested amount; a Goenka-tradition (dhamma.org) course funded entirely by voluntary donation from past students.

foodNotes: All meals prepared and served on-site at no charge for the duration of the course; vegetarian meals included throughout, with tea and a light snack available at teatime for first-time students.
workNotes: Old students (those who have completed at least one prior ten-day course) may serve courses or take part in maintenance work as Dhamma service; new students are not required to work during their first course.
